main_text.p: terdum de pecuniis obligat . Sic in testamento siquis Heres esto, vel Lego dixerit, maximas pecunias alienat. Sicverborum fuorum Effecta Magi prædicant: cùm ex carminũ fuorum euentis de vi verborum arguunt. Neque ab hoc loco aliena sunt bona nomina, quæ veteres notabant. Et Cicero in primo de Diuinat. Cùm Imperator (inquit) exercitum, Censor populum lustraret, bonis nominibus ; qui hostias ducerent, eligebātur : quod item in de leētu Consules obseruant, vt primus miles fiat bono nomine.

Quid appellas Proprium dictionis? Proprium dictionis, est vis vocabuli certa & natiua, & penè (vt ait Cicero) cum ipsa re nata: veluti Vagire proprium est infantium: plangere fœminarum : vlulare canum : hinnire equorum: rudere, asinorū: rugire leonum. Sic Orbus proprie dicitur, qui caret oculis. tranlatè qui liberis, aut qui parentibus, aut qui alia re chara priuatus est. Oracula (inquit Cicero) ex eo ipso appellata sunt, quia inest in his deorum oratio. Sic de Finib. 11. Varietas in disparibus coloribus proprie dicitur, sed transfertur in plura disparia. Morbus proprie dicitur in corpore: morbosos tamen veteres dicebant iracundos. Proprie (inquit Cicero) vt Aegrotatio in corpore, sic Aegritudo in animo nomen habet, non secundum à dolore. Et alibi: Vnde iftud tam ἄχυρον[?], valetudini fideliter inseruiendo? cui verbo domicilium est proprium

page.notes: Catchword "in" at the foot right, excluded from the text. Running head printed with spaced capitals, given as DIALECTAE. Doubtful: the Greek word after "tam" reads as ἄχυρον but is marked [?]; "tranlatè" is printed without s and left as printed; "eligebātur" and "leētu" carry macron-like marks taken as printed; "Sicverborum" and "Effecta" are as printed. Long s normalised to s; "iftud" read with long s as "istud" is not changed (printed "iftud" kept as read: "iftud"). Small marks and dots at the lower edge are not printed text and are omitted.
